synthesis:draft.headline: AEMO defines operational demand as an EMMS 'as generated' regional demand term (used in central dispatch) defined by composition (what generation and responses are included or excluded).

document_statements.paraphrase: The paper describes the composition, use and publication of the different types of demands and associated terms used in AEMO’s EMMS Data Model, with a particular focus on 'as generated' demand.
AEMO identifies three key demand definitions used operationally in the NEM: native demand, operational demand and scheduled demand.
The three key demand definitions are based on 'as generated' demand and are used operationally in AEMO’s central dispatch (EMMS) processes on a regional basis.

document_statements.quote: Operational demand differs from native demand in that it generally excludes demand met by non-scheduled wind/solar generation of aggregate capacity < 30 MW, non-scheduled non-wind/non-solar generation and exempt generation.

document_statements.paraphrase: Actual operational demand reported by AEMO includes the measured operational demand reconstituted with an estimate of actual Wholesale Demand Response (WDR), and AEMO estimates regional actual WDR from SCADA telemetry where available or from the previous-interval dispatch target where telemetry is not available.

document_statements.quote: From time to time, retroactive adjustments to actual operational demand may be required.

document_statements.paraphrase: The paper distinguishes 'as generated', 'sent out' and 'as consumed' demand types based on the location of measurement in the electricity network; AEMO’s EMMS demand definitions are expressed on an 'as generated' basis.

citations.quote: This paper describes the composition, use and publication of the different types of demands and associated terms used in AEMO’s Electricity Market Management Systems (EMMS) Data Model
citations.supports: Describes the paper's scope and focus on EMMS 'as generated' demand definitions used operationally.

citations.quote: In essence, there are three key demands. They are: • Native demand. • Operational demand. • Scheduled demand.
citations.supports: Lists the three key demand definitions including operational demand.

citations.quote: It also discusses native, operational and scheduled demand, the three key demand definitions based on “as generated” demand that are used operationally in the NEM.
citations.supports: States that the key demands are based on 'as generated' demand and used operationally.

citations.quote: Operational demand differs from native demand in that it generally excludes demand met by non-scheduled wind/solar generation of aggregate capacity < 30 MW, non-scheduled non-wind/non-solar generation and exempt generation.
citations.supports: Specifies categories of generation/exclusions from operational demand.

citations.quote: Actual operational demand includes the measured operational demand reconstituted with estimated actual WDR.
citations.supports: Explains that reported actual operational demand is reconstituted to include estimated Wholesale Demand Response.

citations.quote: From time to time, retroactive adjustments to actual operational demand may be required.
citations.supports: States that AEMO may apply retroactive MW adjustments to actual operational demand as its best counterfactual estimate.

citations.quote: As shown in Figure 1 below, based on the location of measurement in the electricity network, demand can be broadly classified into: • “As generated” demand. • “Sent out” demand. • “As consumed” demand.
citations.supports: Defines the measurement bases ('as generated', 'sent out', 'as consumed') used in distinguishing demand types.
